text: The authors choose not to define an analogue of the performance gap recovered (PGR) metric of Burns et al. Their reason is that models trained only on easier tasks, especially with RL, sometimes outperform models trained on all difficulty levels, so they report absolute and relative performance instead.
title: Sun et al. decline Burns et al.'s PGR metric because easy-only training can beat full training
